messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: High tail latency detected for service `runtime-api` in eu-west2. p99 > 5s, streaming stalls correlated across multiple clusters. Severity: P1. Pager: Derek (oncall). 14:22 UTC
Derek (oncall): on it, acknowledging. Adding folks: @Ben (network) @Carla (infra) @Alice (sre)
Alice (sre): seeing p95 jump from ~120ms -> ~1.3s and p99 ~6.2s. Streaming tail stalls: backpressure on websocket connections, many resets. Metrics: tokens/sec drops, circuit-breaker tripped on some frontends.
Ben (network): looking at VPC egress NAT metrics for eu-west2. Cloud provider reporting elevated NAT connection drops and retransmit counts starting ~14:10 UTC. No config deploys from infra in that window.
Carla (infra): no cluster deploys from infra either. Host-level CPU/mem fine. Noted an increase in conntrack table occupancy on a subset of nodes.
Derek (oncall): can you paste conntrack dump + ss?
Ben (network): attaching quick snippets:
```
# ss -s (excerpt)
TCP:   14200 total,  4500 established,  7600 timewait,  1200 orphan
Syncookies: 1 used, 0 dropped
# conntrack -S (summary)
entries: 675k used, conntrack-max: 700k
```
Looks close to exhaustion. Also seeing TLS handshake RTTs spike (many retransmits).
Alice (sre): that explains streaming stalls — TLS handshake delays cause long head-of-line waits for websocket upgrades. Any DNS flaps?
Ben (network): DNS looks okay. This pattern matches NAT ephemeral port exhaustion and packet drops between AZs causing retransmits and handshake stalls. Provider status page shows intermittent NAT hardware issue in eu-west2 zone B->C.
Frank (support): customers reporting degraded streaming: ticket #CS-8421, CS-8422, CS-8423. Two customers experienced reconnect loops. Impact: live transcript feature delayed and partial responses. Not full request failures but long tails.
Derek (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) shift egress for affected subnets to alternate NAT gateways in same region but different AZ; 2) increase conntrack max and net.netfilter nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established temporarily; 3) pin critical routes to avoid cross-zone hairpinning. Applying now.
Carla (infra): implementing sysctl bump: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1000000` and `sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=1024` on frontends in eu-west2-a/b/c. Rolling out via orchestration.
Ben (network): performing route update to prefer nat-gw-2 (eu-west2-b) for VPC routes for prefixes used by frontends. Command: `aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-zzz --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0bbb` (applied to affected route-tables).
Derek (oncall): also scaling NAT capacity: requested provider increase and spun up additional managed NAT instances where possible.
Alice (sre): after sysctl & route change, p95 improved within ~6m: p95 ~200ms, p99 trending down to ~800ms. Streaming stalls count dropped by ~70% in the first 10m.
Ben (network): confirmed packet loss on the inter-AZ path earlier (0.8-1.5% for short windows) and high handshake retransmit counts. After routing change, packet loss on new path is ~0.02%.
Frank (support): notifying impacted customers: short note sent to CS-8421/8422/8423; we offered hotfix guidance and status updates. No data loss reported.
Eve (product): any production feature flags we should flip to reduce load on runtime-api during mitigation?
Derek (oncall): enabling degraded-mode for non-critical streaming features: `deactivate-feature live-transcript` for eu-west2 while we fully remediate. That reduces pressure by ~15%.
Ben (network): also temporarily increased ephemeral port range on frontends: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='15000 65535'` to reduce exhaustion.
Alice (sre): rolling restarts avoided; we prefer sysctl + route changes. No customer-facing downtime needed.
Carla (infra): orchestration confirmed sysctl applied to 95% of targets; NAT scale-up in progress.
Derek (oncall): summary for next shift: suspected root cause - intermittent hardware/firmware failure on cloud provider NAT path causing packet drops and TLS handshake retransmits; symptoms - conntrack nearing capacity, TLS handshake p99 spike, streaming stalls; mitigations applied - increased conntrack, expanded ephemeral ports, route pinning to alternate NAT, scaled NAT capacity, feature flag degraded-mode.
Alice (sre): monitoring: set alert thresholds to p95 > 500ms and p99 > 2s to catch regressions. Created short eval prompt set to validate streaming health.
Ben (network): opened ticket with provider referencing NAT hw fault; case ID: PROVIDER-998245. They acknowledge and are investigating firmware resets in eu-west2-B.
Derek (oncall): passing to next oncall (Alice) at 15:00 UTC. Handoff notes: all mitigations in place, metrics improving but keep provider ticket open and monitor conntrack headroom. Follow-up items: provider RCA, postmortem, consider long-term: egress autoscale, conntrack autosizing, route-failover automation.
Alice (sre): taking over. I'll maintain cadence and close when p99 < 500ms for 30m.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: p99 now ~420ms, p95 ~160ms. Customer impact reduced. Continuing monitoring.
Derek (oncall): thanks team. Leaving a short ops checklist in #postmortems.
Alice (sre): will draft postmortem and schedule follow-up with provider.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: latency metrics stabilized; automated alert cleared at 15:45 UTC. Record: mitigation actions executed, provider engaged for hardware RCA.
Frank (support): updated customer tickets and sent wrap-up message with link to support notes.
